title: Microsoft Teams: tenant meeting policy for who can start recording and transcription
summary: Hold: the template automation command only reads configuration and cannot enforce the setting. The page also reports the new admin control and configuration roles as undocumented despite the supplied notice and published meeting-policy permissions, and overlooks the notice's statement that existing availability controls still apply.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Teams meeting policy through which administrators control who can start recording and transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription, helping organizations apply consistent meeting settings.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The policy can restrict starting recording and transcription to organisers and co-organisers or extend permission to presenters.
claims.quote: Administrators can restrict these permissions to organizers and co-organizers or extend them to presenters.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Administrators can allow organisers to modify the setting or enforce it so organisers cannot change it.
claims.quote: They can also determine whether meeting organizers can modify these settings or whether they are enforced by policy.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the new tenant policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tenant meeting policy "Who can record and transcribe" administrators policy PowerShell; "Who can record" "meeting policy" "579860". Opened meeting-recording, manage-meeting-recording-options, meeting-templates-sensitivity-labels-policies and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.

claims.claim: Learn documents an organiser choice between organisers and co-organisers, or organisers, co-organisers and presenters.
claims.quote:
Organizers with a Teams Premium license have two options for who can record and transcribe a meeting:
- Organizers and co-organizers
- Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Meeting templates and sensitivity labels can enforce who can record in meetings that use them.
claims.quote: The meeting organizer normally makes this choice when they create the meeting. To restrict recording to organizers in meetings with sensitive information, use a meeting template or sensitivity label to enforce this setting.

claims.claim: Learn still states that there is no admin policy for Who can record, while a meeting policy can disable recording entirely.
claims.quote: Meeting recording can be disabled completely using a meeting policy, but there's no admin policy for Who can record.

claims.claim: MC1560924 was published on 2026-11-20.
claims.quote: Published 2026-11-20; last updated 2026-11-20

claims.claim: The notice places Who can record and transcribe in Recording & transcription within the applicable Teams admin center meeting policy.
claims.quote: A new Who can record and transcribe policy control will be available in the Recording & transcription section of the applicable Teams meeting policy in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The new control is one dropdown containing four combinations of participant scope and organiser override permission.
claims.quote: Administrators can select one of the following four options in a single dropdown:

claims.claim: The default value is Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can change.
claims.quote: The default value is Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can change, which preserves the current behavior.

claims.claim: If administrators do not configure the new policy, existing recording and transcription behaviour remains unchanged.
claims.quote: No action is required. If you do not configure the new policy, existing recording and transcription behavior remains unchanged.

claims.claim: The new control is admin-opt-in: it introduces no new restriction until an administrator configures it.
claims.quote: No action is required. If you do not configure the new policy, existing recording and transcription behavior remains unchanged.

claims.claim: Microsoft says no action is required.
claims.quote: No action is required.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label configuring this option takes precedence over the meeting policy.
claims.quote: A sensitivity label that configures this option takes precedence over the meeting policy.

claims.claim: A locked meeting policy takes precedence over a meeting template.
claims.quote: A locked meeting policy takes precedence over a meeting template. An unlocked policy supplies a default.

claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.

claims.quote: General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in late December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

claims.quote: General Availability (GCC High): We will begin rolling out in mid-February 2027 and expect to complete by late February 2027.

claims.quote: General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-February 2027 and expect to complete by early March 2027.

claims.claim: The new policy applies to meetings organised by users assigned that policy.
claims.quote: This provides a centrally managed default or enforced restriction for meetings organized by users assigned the policy, reducing the need for per-meeting configuration.

claims.claim: Both the organiser and recording initiator require recording permissions under the existing recording policy.

claims.quote: When organizers turn off Microsoft Copilot in Teams meetings and events, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: controls[0]; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: The new tenant control has neither a documented admin UI nor documented automation, so both control sides are null.
claims.quote: A new Who can record and transcribe policy control will be available in the Recording & transcription section of the applicable Teams meeting policy in the Teams admin center.
claims.fix: Keep controls[0].api null, but set controls[0].ui.surface to 'Teams admin center', path to 'Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Who can record and transcribe', and docs to 'https://admin.microsoft.com/Adminportal/Home#/MessageCenter/:/messages/MC1560924'. The existing cited meeting-recording page supplies the navigation to a policy and MC1560924 supplies the new control's final steps. Say this is the announced rollout path, not a control already launched. Remove the admin-centre-path question from Open questions, retaining the PowerShell question.

Opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and searched its full text for WhoCan, who can record and recording/transcription; no role-selection setter was documented. Also read meeting-recording and MC1560924.

claims.claim: Meeting recording is configured in Teams admin center at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting recording.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Turn the Meeting recording toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCloudRecording $true enables recording for that policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowCloudRecording $true

claims.claim: Meeting transcription is configured in Teams admin center at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true enables transcription for that policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Template Who can record is reached through Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting templates > Add > Recording & transcription > Who can record.
claims.quote:
expand Meetings and select Meeting templates.
2. Select Add.
### Recording & transcription
Who can record | Specifies whether meetings can be recorded by organizers and co-organizers only or by organizers, co-organizers, and presenters.

claims.claim: Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration is the automation operation for configuring who can record through a template.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet fetches the custom meeting templates stored on the tenant.
Note: This configuration is read only and will only have the Global instance.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api to null and remove the read-only Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration call from the automation cell. Keep the note that no setter was found; do not substitute a getter for a setting operation.

claims.claim: Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration only fetches templates and their meeting options.
claims.quote: Fetches the list of custom templates on the tenant. Each template object contains its list of meeting options, the name of the template, and its ID.

claims.claim: No setter was found for the template's Who can record option.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting templates PowerShell set custom meeting template recording configuration; "TeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration" "Set". Read Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration, create-custom-meeting-template and search excerpts; no matching setter found. AutoRecordingTemplate is for call queues.

claims.claim: The printed Purview label path reaches the wizard for configuring Who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote:
On the Choose protection settings for types of items you selected page, select Protect Teams meetings and chats, and then select Next.
On the Settings for Teams meetings and chats page
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Solutions > Information protection > Labels > Create a label > Define the scope for this label > Choose protection settings for types of items you selected > Protect Teams meetings and chats > Settings for Teams meetings and chats > Control who can record and transcribe'. The current path stops early on the correct wizard page; the note already supplies the remaining setting.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label name> -TeamsWhoCanRecord <value> modifies the sensitivity label's recording-role setting.

claims.claim: Label configuration selects Files & other data assets, Emails and Meetings, then Control who can record and transcribe in Settings for Teams meetings and chats.

make sure Files & other data assets, Emails, and Meetings are selected.
Select Control who can record and transcribe and choose Organizers and co-organizers from the dropdown list.

claims.claim: A label's Who can record and transcribe option does not take effect in Meet Now meetings.
claims.quote:
The following meeting options won't take effect for a Meet Now meeting:
- Who can record and transcribe

claims.claim: Preventing recording entirely uses recording policies, not the template or sensitivity-label Who can record option.
claims.quote: If you need to prevent meetings and events from being recorded entirely, you must use the recording policies in the Teams admin center. This setting applies to the people or groups that you specify, but can't be applied through a meeting template or sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Transcription is both a per-organiser and per-user availability policy.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The new policy remains subject to existing recording and transcription availability controls and any sensitivity label configuring the option.
claims.quote: These configurations remain subject to existing recording and transcription availability controls and any sensitivity label that configures this option.

claims.claim: Custom meeting policies can be assigned to groups separately from the Global policy, enabling a group pilot.
claims.quote:
To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.
To groups: Go to the Group policy assignment tab, select Add, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: On with saved transcript required is an existing enforceable Copilot policy setting.
claims.quote: The only Copilot policy setting that you can enforce is On with saved transcript required.
